**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run the fixing action on a fresh runner**

Whenever analysis finds an actionable issue, this becomes the second `openai/codex-action` invocation in the same `iteration` job after the earlier analysis invocation used `safety-strategy: drop-sudo`. The [documentation for the pinned action](https://github.com/openai/codex-action/blob/bdf19a4a223ec2549a3e2274a0cf61556bc07675/README.md#safety-strategy) explicitly states that invoking the action again with a prompt after sudo has been removed fails and that subsequent work must use a fresh job, so every actionable review will fail here before producing a fix.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match ref-qualified workflow paths**

The workflow-runs REST response qualifies `path` with the workflow ref—for example, the [GitHub REST documentation for this API version](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs?apiVersion=2022-11-28) shows `.github/workflows/build.yml@main`. Therefore a real successful Validate plugin run will not equal the bare `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, leaving `validation` undefined and every clean PR permanently in `WAITING_FOR_CI`; compare the path before `@` or identify the workflow by ID instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Isolate validation and publishing from Codex**

When an actionable review reaches this step, the workspace-write Codex process has just run on the same host, after which this job validates and later commits/pushes the checkout with `AGENT_LOOP_TOKEN`. Under prompt injection, Codex can leave a background process that waits until validation completes and then mutates the workspace before `finish` commits it; the [pinned action's security guidance](https://github.com/openai/codex-action/blob/bdf19a4a223ec2549a3e2274a0cf61556bc07675/docs/security.md#recommendation-run-openaicodex-action-as-the-last-step-in-a-job) specifically warns that processes may remain after the action exits and recommends making the action the last step and transferring its output to a new job. Validation and publication should therefore occur on a fresh runner.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invalidate processed reviews when their context changes**

When a new Codex reply or inline source is added under the same review ID after a clean snapshot, the fingerprint no longer matches, but `reviewDecision` returns `duplicate` because the review was already marked processed and this early return occurs before `removeReady` or any state reset. Consequently an existing `agent-ready` label remains stale, while a PR in `WAITING_FOR_CI` can never resume because later `workflow_run` events also return without reanalysis; a changed fingerprint must invalidate the processed snapshot before review-ID deduplication.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate findings before resolving fixed threads**

If a Codex inline comment is edited while the fixing action or validation is running, this loop resolves the thread using the stale source ID from `plan.json` without re-fetching and comparing the review context, unlike the clean path below. The resulting push may not address the edited finding, yet its thread is still marked resolved and omitted from future contexts; verify that each source body/discussion still matches the analyzed fingerprint before resolving it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resume readiness after every relevant CI completion**

When `Validate plugin` completes while another workflow check or external status is still pending, `ciGreen` correctly leaves the PR in `WAITING_FOR_CI`, but this trigger never runs again when that other check finishes. GitHub's [`workflow_run` documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_run) confirms that a `workflows` list triggers only for the named workflows, and external status completion produces no matching event, so the PR remains stuck until an unrelated event or manual dispatch occurs; subscribe to every readiness-changing event or otherwise schedule a recheck.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
